SpikeGLX Synchronisation Issue

electrophysiology
synchronization
QC
Neuropixels
spikeglx
Cause, impact, correction and wheel validation.
Author

Olivier Winter

Published

November 10, 2026

In 69 Neuropixels recordings, 17 of them in the Brain Wide Map release, the probe sync file is missing its first sync edges. Every spike is shifted against behaviour by a whole multiple of 0.5 s. Behaviour and video are correct. The shift can be inferred from the SpikeGLX metadata, and the wheel confirms it on every recording where it can be tested.

probe recordings audited (12 labs, Aug 2019 – Nov 2026) 4,780
shifted by k × 0.5 s (missing edges at start) 69
of which in the BWM release (590 3B insertions) 17
shifted with SpikeGLX 20221012 or later 0

What it looks like

Trial-aligned activity from the IBL viz site. In an aligned recording, responses lock to stimulus, movement and feedback at 0 s. In a shifted recording, the whole raster moves by the shift: +0.5 s puts the feedback response at +0.5 s, and −1.5 s pushes every response out of the plotted window, so the raster looks flat.

Impact on the Brain Wide Map

17 of the 590 3B insertions in the BWM release are shifted. The 109 Neuropixels 3A insertions have no nidq file and are outside this census.

  • 13 come from one UCLA rig over two months in 2023. They are shifted by +0.5 s, except one at −1.5 s.
  • 4 are sporadic whole-second shifts: NYU-12, SWC_039, ibl_witten_29, and UCLA034 on the same rig in 2022, before the problem.
  • For all 17, the offset of the population spiking rate corrleated with the wheel agrees with the shift to within 0.11 s.
Warning

Any analysis that aligns spikes to task events is affected on these insertions: PSTHs, and decoding or encoding of stimulus, choice, movement and feedback. A 0.5 s shift moves feedback responses into the next epoch. Shifts of 1 s or more remove task-locked responses from typical analysis windows.

Other projects

52 more recordings outside the BWM release have the same signature.

  • 38 come from the same UCLA rig, 33 of them from MM012 (three probes per session).
  • 14 are sporadic, mostly in the Witten lab dopamine project (dop_47 to dop_53, −1 to −7 s).
  • Wheel check: of the 44 with spike sorting, 42 confirm the metadata shift to within 0.09 s. Two have a wheel correlation too weak to tell (KS075, MFD_09 2023-10-18), and none contradicts it.
  • Not testable: 8 recordings, six without spike sorting and two without a registered insertion. CSH_ZAD_021 2020-06-15 probe01 has a −105 s shift (210 missing edges) and is among them.

Root cause

Older versions of spikeGLX (before 20221012) had sporadic instances of “mistarts” where first edges were missing (18, 4 of them BWM, multiple labs). This has been fixed in 20221012. However in UCLA, one rig did get a firmware upgrade while staying on the older spikeGLX version, resulting in a systematic shift. This represents 51 sessions from a single rig, 13 of them BWM.

Sporadic cases (18 recordings / 4 of which BWM)

18 recordings are spread over 6 labs from 2019 to 2022, on SpikeGLX 20190327, 20190413 and 20201103. In all of them, the probe file misses an even number of edges at the start. The shift is therefore a whole number of seconds and always negative (spikes early). We have not found a common hardware or software cause.

The UCLA rig (51 recordings / 13 of which BWM)

All 51 shifted recordings on the Churchland lab UCLA rig share one combination: SpikeGLX 20201103 running on base-station firmware 2.0.169 with connect-card firmware 3.2.186. That combination was used only from 15 Aug to 20 Oct 2023, and every recording made with it is shifted.

  • Up to 13 Aug 2023: old firmware 3.2.176, 322 recordings. Only one is shifted (UCLA034 2022-01-25, a sporadic case). MFD_05 recordings before the upgrade are aligned.
  • 14–15 Aug 2023: the firmware upgrade lands. From then on, every recording made with SpikeGLX 20201103 is shifted, mostly by +0.5 s. MM012 sessions alternate between +0.5 and −0.5 s.
  • 29 Aug 2023: the headstage, flex and probe on MFD_07 are swapped (headstage firmware 5.1 → 5.3, flex 1.2 → 4.13). The first run on the new hardware is shifted by −1.5 s, with firstSample off the 0.5 s grid. From 30 Aug it is back to +0.5 s.
  • 20 Oct 2023: last shifted recording (MFD_09).

Firmware 3.2.186 alone is not the cause. From 14 Aug, the same base station also recorded 490 sessions with SpikeGLX 20230411 (MM009 to MM015, MM012 included), and none is shifted. Both versions were in use on that base station over the same weeks, and only the old version on the new firmware shifts. The new firmware probably came with SpikeGLX 20230411, and the old version kept being launched against it. This is inferred from the dates and has not been confirmed with the lab.

Mechanism

SpikeGLX records a 1 Hz square wave on both the nidq (behaviour) and the probe streams, with an edge every 0.5 s. ibllib (version3B) pairs the edges of the two streams by index, starting from the first. The specification states that the edges are aligned from the start: “With sync enabled, SpikeGLX uses the edges so that files in a new set all start at a common wall time”

When this is not the case, every pair is off by k edges and spikes shift by k × 0.5 s. The edges still pair one-to-one and regularly, so the sync QC passes.

Methods

Validation against the wheel

The wheel is recorded on the nidq clock and is not periodic, so cross-correlating the population firing rate with wheel speed measures the true offset directly. Aligned recordings peak just below 0 s, because neural activity leads movement by tens of milliseconds. We subtract that baseline, taken as the median over 30 aligned BWM insertions.

Detection and correction from the metadata

For each recording we compare the two streams’ fileTimeSecs and sync edge counts. A recording that is missing edges at the start shows all three of these:

  1. the file durations differ by dT, with k = round(dT / 0.5 s) ≠ 0;
  2. the edge counts differ by exactly k;
  3. the edges are otherwise regular (every interval between 0.25 and 0.75 s) and complete at both ends.

The correction is to pair the edges from the last one, which drops the first |k| edges of the longer stream. Spikes then move by k × 0.5 s. No raw data and no re-sorting are needed.

Note

The edges alone cannot say whether the missing edges are at the start (a shift) or at the end (a truncated file, no shift), so the wheel was used to check. Every testable case was a shift.

In SpikeGLX 20221012 and later: the firstSample field is reliable and settles it. These 1,432 recordings show no shift and one truncation (KM_041).

## Root cause

Older versions of spikeGLX (before `20221012`) had sporadic instances of "mistarts" where first edges were missing (18, 4 of them BWM, multiple labs). 
This has been fixed in `20221012`. However in UCLA, one rig did get a firmware upgrade while staying on the older spikeGLX version, resulting 
in a systematic shift. This represents 51 sessions from a single rig, 13 of them BWM.

### Sporadic cases (18 recordings / 4 of which BWM)

18 recordings are spread over 6 labs from 2019 to 2022, on SpikeGLX `20190327`, `20190413` and `20201103`.
In all of them, the probe file misses an even number of edges at the start. The shift is therefore a whole number of
seconds and always negative (spikes early). We have not found a common hardware or software cause.

### The UCLA rig (51 recordings / 13 of which BWM)

All 51 shifted recordings on the Churchland lab UCLA rig share one combination: SpikeGLX `20201103` running on
base-station firmware `2.0.169` with connect-card firmware `3.2.186`. That combination was used only from 15 Aug to
20 Oct 2023, and every recording made with it is shifted.

- **Up to 13 Aug 2023:** old firmware `3.2.176`, 322 recordings. Only one is shifted (UCLA034 2022-01-25, a sporadic
  case). MFD_05 recordings before the upgrade are aligned.
- **14–15 Aug 2023:** the firmware upgrade lands. From then on, every recording made with SpikeGLX `20201103` is
  shifted, mostly by +0.5 s. MM012 sessions alternate between +0.5 and −0.5 s.
- **29 Aug 2023:** the headstage, flex and probe on MFD_07 are swapped (headstage firmware 5.1 → 5.3, flex
  1.2 → 4.13). The first run on the new hardware is shifted by −1.5 s, with `firstSample` off the 0.5 s grid.
  From 30 Aug it is back to +0.5 s.
- **20 Oct 2023:** last shifted recording (MFD_09).

Firmware `3.2.186` alone is not the cause. From 14 Aug, the same base station also recorded 490 sessions with SpikeGLX
`20230411` (MM009 to MM015, MM012 included), and none is shifted. Both versions were in use on that base station over
the same weeks, and only the old version on the new firmware shifts. The new firmware probably came with SpikeGLX
`20230411`, and the old version kept being launched against it. This is inferred from the dates and has not been
confirmed with the lab.

![Churchland lab UCLA probes in 2023, by SpikeGLX version and connect-card firmware. Only `20201103` on `3.2.186` (bottom row, red) is shifted.](figures/churchland_timeline.png)

### Mechanism

SpikeGLX records a 1 Hz square wave on both the nidq (behaviour) and the probe streams, with an edge every 0.5 s.
`ibllib` (`version3B`) pairs the edges of the two streams by index, starting from the first. The specification states
that the edges are aligned from the start: ["With sync enabled, SpikeGLX uses the edges so that files in a new set all start at a common wall time"](https://billkarsh.github.io/SpikeGLX/help/syncEdges/Sync_edges/)

When this is not the case, every pair is off by *k* edges and spikes shift by *k* × 0.5 s. The edges still pair one-to-one and regularly, so the sync QC passes.
![The probe file misses the first edge. Pairing by index from the start (red) is off by one edge; pairing from the last edge (green) is correct.](figures/sync_pairing.svg)


## Methods

### Validation against the wheel

The wheel is recorded on the nidq clock and is not periodic, so cross-correlating the population firing rate with
wheel speed measures the true offset directly. Aligned recordings peak just below 0 s, because neural activity leads
movement by tens of milliseconds. We subtract that baseline, taken as the median over 30 aligned BWM insertions.

![Rate–wheel cross-correlation. Shifted recordings peak at −1 s (NYU-12, UCLA034) and +0.5 s (MFD_07). Siblings and controls recorded alongside peak near 0 s.](figures/006_wheel_xcorr.png)

![Wheel offset against the shift inferred from the metadata, 61 recordings. 59 lie within 0.11 s of the identity line (grey band, right). The 2 open circles have a weak wheel correlation (SNR < 2).](figures/015_wheel_vs_shift.png)


### Detection and correction from the metadata

For each recording we compare the two streams' `fileTimeSecs` and sync edge counts. A recording that is missing edges
at the start shows all three of these:

1. the file durations differ by *dT*, with *k* = round(*dT* / 0.5 s) ≠ 0;
2. the edge counts differ by exactly *k*;
3. the edges are otherwise regular (every interval between 0.25 and 0.75 s) and complete at both ends.

The correction is to pair the edges from the last one, which drops the first |*k*| edges of the longer stream. Spikes
then move by *k* × 0.5 s. No raw data and no re-sorting are needed.

::: {.callout-note}
The edges alone cannot say whether the missing edges are at the start (a shift) or at the end (a truncated file, no
shift), so the wheel was used to check. Every testable case was a shift.

In **SpikeGLX `20221012` and later:** the `firstSample` field is reliable and settles it. These 1,432 recordings show no shift and one truncation (KM_041).
:::
